newsitem.title: CANADA: TrizecHahn launches airport joint venture.
newsitem.headline: TrizecHahn launches airport joint venture.

text.p: TrizecHahn Corp on Wednesday said it has formed a joint venture aimed at developing, expanding and managing airports and airport terminals worldwide.
The Toronto-based real estate company formed the joint venture with Airport Development Corp (ADC), a unit of Toronto-based Huang & Danczkay Properties, a privately held firm.

TrizecHahn did not specify the potential cash value of the joint venture. The company said a trend towards airport privatization and strong growth in air passenger traffic meant there were significant opportunities in the industry.
"Airport development is a unique opportunity that offers outstanding long-term potential," said TrizecHahn chief executive Peter Munk, in a statement.

ADC is known for developing the US$600 million Trillium Terminal 3 at Toronto's Pearson International Airport and will begin construction this spring of a new terminal at Ferihegy Airport in Budapest, Hungary, TrizecHahn said.

TrizecHahn said airport development is a growth industry and noted 50 countries have announced plans to privatize commercial airports. Industry forecasts estimate that up to US$400 billion of airport development will occur in the next 15 years, the company said.

"The combination of our expertise and financial strength with ADC's airport experience gives our new joint venture a significant competitive advantage," said TrizecHahn president Gregory Wilkins in a statement.

TrizecHahn will be "very committed" to the new joint venture and airport development is now part of the company's long-term development strategy, Laurie Ludwick, director of media relations for TrizecHahn told Reuters.
TrizecHahn shares were unchanged at the close of trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange. More than 360,000 shares had changed hands.
